text: deh-remote 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的局域网远程控制插件。它在侧边栏提供手机入口和配对面板，主机端生成限时配对二维码，并通过本机局域网转发器让手机连接到现有 Web GUI。配对后手机使用官方界面，并启用纵向触控适配；桌面端可以查看配对设备、复制配对链接、停止配对或撤销设备。设置页可启停远程能力和局域网访问，并调整配对时限及设备限制。使用需运行 DSH Web，并让手机与主机处于可互通的局域网；插件还会按日向 dsh-market.com 发送匿名安装心跳。

deh-remote lets a phone use DSH Web over a local network. Scan the host pairing panel’s time-limited QR code to open the official GUI with portrait touch support. Users can view paired devices and revoke access. Settings control LAN access. A daily anonymous install heartbeat goes to dsh-market.com.

deh-remote 的功能「手机二维码配对」：桌面侧边栏打开配对面板后显示限时二维码和链接；手机扫码后进入 DSH 官方 Web 界面，并可查看或撤销已配对设备。
deh-remote 使用前须知：客户端每日最多发送一次匿名安装心跳至 dsh-market.com，内容含包名、版本（如有）及随机访客标识；可由全局遥测退出项或浏览器 DNT 抑制。

text: @echo-125/deh-remote README · @echo-125/deh-remote · LAN-only Remote Web Control for DeepSeek Harness (DSH)：> Remote control of the DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Web GUI over the local area network, with both ends running the **exact same official interface**: pair an iPhone, Android smartphone, tablet, or another computer from the QR code next to settings. Phones receive an injected portrait touch layer while remote computers enjoy the complete desktop workbench, and access is guarded by expiring pairing tokens plus revocable device sessions. Reachability is LAN only: the host keeps its loopback bind, a runtime forwarder serves this machine's LAN address, and there is no public-access path.

@echo-125/deh-remote README · Origin and scope：- **Origin**: copied out of the monorepo as its own repository, renamed to tell it apart
  from the original (`@echo-125/deh-remote`).
- **Scope**: **LAN-only** remote control — no tunnel, no relay, no public base URL, and
  the master switch `enabled` is off by default. Pairing grants full control, but
  `/api/update` and `/api/plugin-manager` stay on loopback and never ride the
  `/remote` channel.
- **The phone runs the same official Web GUI** — there is no second interface to drift.
- **This round of changes** (see [PROJECT_HISTORY.md](PROJECT_HISTORY.md)): the tunnel
  answers WebSocket Pongs on the phone's behalf, the browser APIs Safari only gained in
  17.4 are polyfilled, the channel reconnects as soon as the page resumes, and the
  host traces the channel so a phone can read the diagnosis without DevTools.

@echo-125/deh-remote README · Origin and scope：---
This package is an official external plugin for DeepSeek Harness (DSH), structured as a cordis bundle: the host half manages pairing tokens, device sessions, `/api/pair` routes, the gated `/remote` channel, the LAN forwarder and the matching host firewall rule; the browser half renders the remote access trigger, QR pairing modal, live device roster, settings card, and mobile portrait touch adaptation.

@echo-125/deh-remote README · Workspaces on a phone：A phone cannot operate a desktop file dialog, so the remote channel does not ask
for one: "Add workspace" and "New session" both land in the **default
workspace** - the one the host itself resolves on first use (the account
Documents directory plus a fixed leaf). The desktop keeps its own chooser; only
the remote origin is redirected.

@echo-125/deh-remote README · Diagnosing a connection：- **A host-side trace** of every mux upgrade attempt (path, whether the credential
  was accepted, the gate verdict, the inner handshake status, the survival time),
  written under the DSH home while the diagnostics are armed.
- **A server-rendered page** at `/pair-diag`, readable from the phone or the
  desktop, and a banner on the landing page when the diagnostics are on.
- **A panel on the page** that shows the connection state, the generation, the
  transport shape and every leg - plus the official client's own messages, which
  name the reason a generation never becomes ready.

@echo-125/deh-remote README · The mobile adaptation layer：The official desktop layout already auto-collapses the sidebar below 1024px. On top of that, while the viewport is portrait + coarse pointer + narrower than 1100px the plugin injects:

@echo-125/deh-remote README · The mobile adaptation layer：The paired remote desktop also runs in **host mode**: on this harness line the "configuration plane is local" behavior is a client-side branch on `connection.isLoopback`, and the channel boot script installs the transport hook (`__DSH_TRANSPORT__.ownsHost = true`) before any boot entry. Host mode is **server-granted**: the hook is installed only when the device-gated app landing (`/pair-app`) published the grant marker ahead of the boot patch, so a shell served to an unpaired browser — a fence-open deployment — never poses as the machine owner. Settings, credentials, agent presets, and deliverables therefore work on the phone exactly as on the desktop — every call still rides the gated `/remote` channel. The gated channel keeps three path families physically local: `/api/pair/*`, `/api/update/*`, and `/api/plugin-manager/*`.

@echo-125/deh-remote README · Harness contract dependencies：- **`sidebar.footer.action` foot seat** (the 0.1.7 shell composition): the sidebar declares and renders the seat the remote entry occupies.
- **`ctx.layout.toggleSidebar()`** (packages/client/ui-layout): the whale button expands the collapsed sidebar through the official panel-action face.
- **`ctx.connection.authenticatedUrl()`** (packages/client/connection): the sanctioned launch-token seam the proxy redeems once for its inner credential (`src/inner-auth.ts`), so re-issued `/api` calls satisfy the harness browser-auth check.
- **`__DSH_FILE_UPLOAD__`** (file-upload client hooks): the optional pre-Cordis transport the upload service reads once at construction. The remote boot patch publishes it so background uploads stay on the rewritten main-thread fetch instead of a Web Worker that escapes the channel (issue #1580).
- **`__DSH_TRANSPORT__.ownsHost`** (client-connection transport hooks): the host-mode flip for paired remote desktops. It is installed only when the device-gated app landing published the `__DSH_REMOTE_HOST_GRANT__` marker ahead of the boot patch, so the flip is server-granted rather than asserted from the o

@echo-125/deh-remote README · Harness contract dependencies：The fence helpers (`isTrustedApiRequest` / `isLoopbackHostname`) are reimplemented locally in `src/gate.ts` / `src/routes.ts`: the connection plugin stopped exporting them, so the pairing routes carry their own copy scoped to the literals the QR links advertise. The loopback question is split in two there: `isLoopbackUpstream` (loopback socket and Host, forwarding headers ignored) only decides whether a Host can be answered at all, while `isLoopbackClient` (no forwarding header) decides who receives a credential or the desktop payload. The shared copy in `shared/host/loopback.ts` keeps `isLoopbackRequest` refusing every forwarded request and adds `isForwardedLoopbackRequest` for the narrower shape a route family may admit behind its own default-off switch.

@echo-125/deh-remote README · Security model：- **Pairing is the access control for the `/remote` channel, unconditionally**: every request must carry a live paired-device cookie, enforced before any bytes are forwarded. A missing or revoked session receives HTTP 403 with a JSON rejection carrying `error.code: "unpaired"`; the browser's `EventSource` API exposes only the stream failure, not that response body. This gate does **not** follow `requirePairingForLan`: the channel re-issues every call with the process's own browser-auth credential, so admitting an unpaired caller would hand out that authority. The LAN policy governs the plain `/api` surface only and can never widen the channel (issue #1665).
- **The channel carries the process's own inner credential.** The harness browser-auth cookie is authority-bound (minted for the exact `host:port` a browser visited) and has no loopback exemption, so a proxied re-issue to `127.0.0.1` cannot reuse a device's cookie. The plugin therefore redeems its own launch token once — the same exchange a first browser visit performs — and attaches that cookie to re-issued requests. The credential is only ever exercised behind the pairing gate above

@echo-125/deh-remote README · Known Limitations and Deferred Work：- **The LAN entry follows the forwarder, not a profile write**: the toggle starts and stops it while the process runs, so nothing here needs a restart; after a network change, flip it off and on again. The port follows the web server's own port, so restarting the desktop can move it. A LAN address that has gone away, or a port already taken, costs the LAN entry only — the loopback listener is untouched and the status frame reports `forward.reason` (`off`, `host-bind`, or `no-address`) with `forward.error`.
- **A legacy managed block is removed once, and one of its shapes still needs a hand**: a block written by this plugin up to 0.4.8 is stripped on the first activation of each process — atomically, only when it is actually there, with the file's permissions preserved and nothing written back — and `legacyBlockRemoved` reports it. The cleanup runs when the plugin activates, so an updated build takes it on the next `dsh web` start. The exception is a block that pinned `0.0.0.0`: DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 and later refuse that value before this plugin ever loads, so that host cannot reach the cleanup. Edit the profile's `cordis.p

@echo-125/deh-remote README · Dependency rationale：`qrcode.react` (MIT, actively maintained, React 16–19 support) renders the QR as a dependency-free SVG component — no canvas, no server-side image generation. It is inlined into the client bundle at build time (like the official skin/turtle-ui plugins inline their non-shared deps), so profile installations need no extra runtime dependency beyond the dsh peer closure. `schemastery` is the DSH-standard config schema validator.
